assertion.rationale: F7: verify jobs — a nonsecurity function, read-only auditing — declare environment: demo and id-token: write while intending to run as the Reader-scoped verifier. Because the OIDC subject derives from the job's environment name rather than the client-id passed to azure/login, these nominally non-privileged jobs actually federate to the Owner-capable deployer identity, so a non-privileged (audit) function is never actually accessing the system through a non-privileged account or role.

recommendation: Move verify jobs to a dedicated verify environment federated only to mls-verifier (Reader), distinct from the demo environment used for deploys, so nonsecurity/audit functions run under a genuinely non-privileged identity.
